plans.note: Section 15 is headed 'Limitation of Garman's Liability' — one-sided framing suggests checking mutuality, cap size (likely tied to fees paid) and carve-outs for IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct. Text may continue onto the PAGE 8 marker section.

Section 13 provides the IP indemnity from Garman; confirm scope (defence, settlement, replace/refund remedy), absence of a reciprocal customer indemnity, and that any liability cap in sec-15 does not swallow it.

No non-compete heading; restrictions in sec-3 are use restrictions on the software rather than restraints on our business. Confirm nothing in sec-3 or the general matters clauses bars us from acquiring or developing competing routing systems.
Likely absent; check the grant (sec-2), maintenance (sec-10) and fees (sec-11) for any sole-source or exclusive-supplier language before concluding.
No pricing-parity heading; scan fees (sec-11) and maintenance charges (sec-10) for any obligation running from us to Garman. MFN in our favour would be acceptable and not flagged.

Section 19 is on point. Check mutuality, duration (12 months preferred, 24 fallback), scope limited to individuals involved in the engagement, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Section 17 (term and termination) is primary; the option to reject (sec-7, sec-8) and maintenance cancellation in sec-10 may give us early-exit rights. Confirm we can exit on notice without penalty and that Garman cannot terminate maintenance mid-term for convenience.

Maintenance is the likely auto-renewing element — check sec-10 and sec-17 for the renewal term, the non-renewal notice window (30–60 days preferred) and any uncapped uplift in the sec-11 fee provisions.

Governing law and venue will sit in the general matters clause; text may run across the PAGE 10/11 markers. Verify the chosen law is an accepted jurisdiction and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.

Assignment is normally in sec-20 general matters; also check sec-2 for licence transfer limits and sec-17 for any termination right triggered by our change of control. We need affiliate/successor assignment without consent.

Garman retains software IP (sec-2/sec-3), which is expected; the review point is ownership of our data (data conversion in sec-4), any modifications or configurations we pay for, and that sec-14 confidentiality does not vest our information in Garman. Escrow (sec-16) is supportive.

Section 2 grant read with the sec-1 definitions (Authorized Locations) and sec-3 restrictions. Confirm the licence is perpetual/irrevocable once fees are paid and extends to affiliates and outsourced contractors at each authorized location.

Any verification right against our usage would sit with the sec-3 use restrictions or in sec-20 general matters; if present, test notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost. Flag as missing only if no verification language appears.

Look for late-payment interest or stipulated damages in sec-11 and any termination charges in sec-17; commercially reasonable interest is not a liquidated-damages deviation. Service credits in our favour are welcome.

Section 12 is the specifications and warranty clause; read with acceptance testing (sec-6) and maintenance (sec-10). Check the warranty period runs from acceptance, that conformity is to documented specifications, and that repair/replace escalates to refund.

No insurance heading; check general matters and the co-operation/implementation clause (sec-9, on-site work) before recording as missing given Garman personnel will attend our locations and handle data.
Check sec-11 fees and sec-10 maintenance for any committed seat/location minimum or obligation to maintain a minimum spend; licence quantities defined in sec-1 schedules may imply a floor.

Section 17 termination consequences and sec-18 survival are the likely home; source code escrow (sec-16) and the rejection remedy (sec-8) partially cover continuity. Confirm we get our data back in usable form and reasonable exit assistance — if only escrow exists, the rule is likely missing.
